description: Release 1.7.5 value-scoring model for ranking pending roadmap work in portfolio assessment responses. Aggregation semantics settled by operator 2026-07-06 (Release 2.7 Phase A): MAX within a dimension, with an effortFit floor for sprawling items. Model 1.2 adds executor classification (2026-09-11): value and dispatchability are separate questions, so an item only a person can perform keeps its score and leaves the dispatch queue.

effortFitFloor.description: A larger-surface effortFit keyword (score <= cap, e.g. refactor/rewrite/persistent/oauth/distribution/analytics/autonomous) floors effortFit at the lowest matched score even when a bounded verb (add/wire/...) also matched, so sprawling items do not read as bounded one-task work. Operator decision 2026-07-06.

executorClassification.description: Who can actually perform the item. The impact dimension rewards operator-FACING outcomes, which is correct, but it cannot tell them apart from operator-EXECUTED tasks — so before this block existed, manual work outranked agent work in a queue whose whole purpose is dispatching work the operator does not have to do. Classification never changes valueScore; it decides which lane the item belongs in. A declared tag always beats an inferred keyword, because the roadmap author knows and the regex only guesses. Rules are deliberately high-precision: mislabelling agent work as operator work parks something nobody picks up, which is the exact harm this fixes.

operatorRules.pattern: \b(on a (phone|real device|handset|tablet)|over mobile data|in person|in-person|physical (device|hardware|venue)|walk the floor)\b
operatorRules.label: needs a physical device or a person on site
needs a live event with real participants
names a person as the actor

operatorRules.pattern: \b(billing|credit card|payment method|purchase|subscription|domain registration|register a domain|provider console|cloud console|at the (database )?provider)\b
operatorRules.label: needs a third-party account, billing, or provider console action

impact.description: User-visible or operator-visible value delivered by the work item.

unblockPotential.description: How much the item removes a blocker for dispatch, validation, adoption, or later work.

riskReduction.description: Security, reliability, testability, auditability, and operational risk reduction.

repoMaturity.description: How ready the repository is to absorb and validate the work.

effortFit.description: Preference for bounded work items that are likely to complete cleanly in one task.

dependencyReduction.description: How much the item reduces cross-feature, cross-repo, or sequencing dependencies.

recency.description: Roadmap order signal; earlier pending items usually represent the author's intended next step.

unblockPotential.label: removes a readiness or dispatch blocker
reduces signal drift or stale state
